newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian wheat stabilised by rain.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian wheat stabilised by rain.

text.p: Reasonable rainfall since August 7 had stabilised Australia's domestic wheat market and further falls over the next two to three weeks might continue the trend, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday.
The AWB tender results of both Tuesday and Thursday also indicated a softening in demand, it said.
Australia's eastern states, including New South Wales, still required supporting rains to carry the crop and this would continue to have an influence over the coming weeks, it said.
Wheat futures on the Sydney Futures Exchange continued to trade actively during the week, in the mid-A$190.00 a tonne range for Australian Standard White, it said.
Early receivals in Queensland marked the beginning of harvest. This should increase in momentum in coming weeks.
Urgency in the domestic feed market also eased following recent rains, but trading gained momentum as the market speculated on the liklihood of the supporting rain needed to finish the crop, it said.
Sorghum rose another A$10.00 a tonne during the week following strong demand from Queensland and Victorian consumers seeking to cover requirements in the present uncertain supply situation, it said.
